resources.string: Paneth cell release icons in the crypt lumen
Starting icons at the apical side
Icons still on the cell side: %1$s

Luminal icon count = the smaller of the selected arrow count and the starting icon count. Icons left on the cell side = starting icons minus luminal icons. The chart rounds selections to whole counts.

Paneth cells sit at the base of small-intestinal crypts. Their apical granules release material toward the crypt lumen, helping protect the nearby lining. In this drawing, a line separates the apical cell side from the crypt lumen. Each selected arrow can move one available icon across the line. The icons are bookkeeping symbols: they do not depict intact granules crossing the surface, actual quantities, or how much protection the lining receives.
